chunks: And as for what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda' who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: A woman is not married off to her paternal aunt, nor to her maternal aunt, nor to her milk-sister.
The meaning in this report is like the meaning in what preceded regarding the paternal and maternal aunts of lineage, that it is not permissible without consent.
As for with consent, there is no harm in it, similar to that of lineage.
As for marrying her to her milk-sister, it is prohibited in all cases, unless the sister is separated by death or a definitive divorce.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in marriage prohibition rules between aunts of lineage and milk-sisters in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the juristic distinction between consanguineous aunts (paternal and maternal) and milk-sisters, noting that while marriage to aunts of lineage is permissible with the aunt's consent, marriage to a milk-sister is strictly prohibited unless the existing marital bond is severed by death or a final divorce. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the permanence of milk-kinship (radāʿah) in establishing mahram status, contrasting it with the conditional nature of lineage-based prohibitions. The ruling underscores the principle that milk-sisterhood creates an indelible barrier to marriage, mirroring the status of full sisters.
